rationale: Both candidates converge on the same core, diff-grounded bugs (fork_rng's default device_type='cuda' silently mis-forking non-CUDA RNG state, the NPU/XPU allowlist widening from '==cuda' to '!=cpu', and the FL2VA/Ref2VA copy-paste bug in the recipe), and both miss the actual ground-truth reviewer ask (use `current_omni_platform.device` instead of the new device_module pattern), so recall is low and tied. X edges ahead on actionability with ready-to-paste fix diffs and a clean Verdict/Blocking/Nits structure, plus one extra valid finding (device_module attribute being unpicklable); Y is slightly more rigorous with per-finding evidence citations and catches a torch-version-pinning concern X doesn't, but its output is cluttered with irrelevant system/meta text (skill-candidate footer) that a human reviewer wouldn't want.
